answer: Each new identity moors at one harbor berth, posting promised work. Its kernel is that promise: seven neighbors each check one facet, co-sign, and lock 15 credits on a quartz ledger. Each epoch the harbor audit re-checks the kernel; a miss burns 15. A rented-berth ring fails: one shared key exposes it on the quartz ledger. 1,000 fakes need 7,000 signatures at 25 credits: 175,000 vs a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 105, keeping its full share.
